AI.tldr: COBS improves block sparse attention by using second-order statistics (cumulant expansion) for better block selection, closing ~86% of the quality gap to dense attention while maintaining a 15x reduction in KV cache read traffic compared to dense attention.
AI.motivation: Block sparse attention is hardware-friendly but underutilized in leading open-weight LLMs, which prefer dense attention or fine-grained selection. The paper seeks to understand why and proposes a better block selection mechanism to make block sparse attention competitive.
AI.method: The authors formalize block selection as ranking blocks by attention mass (sum of attention scores). They show exact computation requires reading all keys, so the problem reduces to approximating attention mass from a compact summary. Using cumulant expansion, they reveal existing methods use only first-order approximations. COBS extends NSA with a novel selector storing compressed second-order statistics per block.
AI.result: On the 32k RULER benchmark, COBS improves NSA baseline from 0.2999 to 0.8195 (dense: 0.9040), closing ~86% of the gap. It uses only 1.21x the KV cache read traffic of NSA and 15.15x less than dense attention. It also preserves short-context behavior and achieves lower position-wise NLL than dense attention.
AI.conclusion: Block sparse attention can match dense attention quality if blocks are selected by attention mass, but this requires good approximation. Second-order cumulant information significantly improves block selection over first-order methods, making block sparse attention viable for practical LLM deployment.

title: Causally Debiased Latent Action Model for Embodied Action Conditioned World Models
summary: Action-conditioned world models (ACWMs) aim to simulate future observations conditioned on embodied actions, offering a promising foundation for robot planning, policy evaluation, and data augmentation. However, learning controllable ACWMs requires large-scale action-labeled data, which remains costly to collect in the real world. Latent action models (LAMs) mitigate this bottleneck by inferring latent actions from unlabeled videos, but existing LAMs are typically trained with reconstruction-only objectives and therefore entangle action-relevant dynamics with action-irrelevant visual factors such as backgrounds and untouched objects. In this work, we identify this action-irrelevant bias as a key obstacle to controllable ACWMs and introduce evaluation metrics to measure latent-action bias, action following, and robustness. We propose CD-LAM, a causally debiased framework for LAM-based ACWMs. CD-LAM introduces three efficient fine-tuning objectives: embodiment-centric reconstruction, action-centric contrastive learning, and latent space calibration, which together encourage embodiment-focused, action-aware, and calibrated non-collapsed latent action representations. Experiments on 2B and 14B ACWM backbones show that CD-LAM substantially improves latent-action controllability, downstream robot-action following, visual fidelity, and adaptation efficiency, requiring only 6k fine-tuning steps and more than 12$\times$ fewer robot-action adaptation updates than the baseline.

AI.tldr: CD-LAM is a causally debiased framework that improves latent-action controllability in action-conditioned world models by mitigating action-irrelevant biases through three fine-tuning objectives, achieving substantial gains with only 6k steps and 12× fewer adaptation updates.
AI.motivation: Existing latent action models (LAMs) entangle action-relevant dynamics with action-irrelevant visual factors (e.g., backgrounds, untouched objects) due to reconstruction-only training, hindering controllable action-conditioned world models. The paper seeks to identify and eliminate this bias.
AI.method: CD-LAM introduces three fine-tuning objectives: embodiment-centric reconstruction, action-centric contrastive learning, and latent space calibration, applied to LAM-based ACWMs on 2B and 14B backbones.
AI.result: CD-LAM substantially improves latent-action controllability, robot-action following, visual fidelity, and adaptation efficiency, requiring only 6k fine-tuning steps and more than 12× fewer robot-action adaptation updates compared to baselines.
AI.conclusion: Action-irrelevant bias is a key obstacle to controllable ACWMs, and the proposed causally debiased framework effectively addresses it, enabling efficient and controllable world models from unlabeled video.

title: EvoLP: Self-Evolving Latency Predictor for Model Compression in Real-Time Edge Systems
comment: Author's accepted version. Published in IEEE Embedded Systems Letters
summary: Edge devices are increasingly utilized for deploying deep learning applications on embedded systems. The real-time nature of many applications and the limited resources of edge devices necessitate latency-targeted neural network compression. However, measuring latency on real devices is challenging and expensive. Therefore, this letter presents a novel and efficient framework, named EvoLP, to accurately predict the inference latency of models on edge devices. This predictor can evolve to achieve higher latency prediction precision during the network compression process. Experimental results demonstrate that EvoLP outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches by being evaluated on three edge devices and four model variants. Moreover, when incorporated into a model compression framework, it effectively guides the compression process for higher model accuracy while satisfying strict latency constraints. We open source EvoLP at https://github.com/ntuliuteam/EvoLP.

AI.tldr: EvoLP is a latency predictor for edge devices that evolves during network compression to accurately forecast inference latency, outperforming prior methods on three devices and four model variants, and effectively guides compression to maintain accuracy under latency constraints.
AI.motivation: Measuring latency on real edge devices is challenging and expensive, yet necessary for deploying deep learning on resource-limited embedded systems with real-time requirements.
AI.method: EvoLP is an evolvable latency prediction framework that iteratively improves its prediction precision during the network compression process.
AI.result: EvoLP outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches on three edge devices and four model variants; when integrated into model compression, it achieves higher accuracy while satisfying strict latency constraints.
AI.conclusion: EvoLP provides an accurate, evolving latency predictor that effectively guides latency-constrained neural network compression for edge devices.

title: HiHR: Hierarchical Hyperbolic Representation for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification
comment: Accepted by ECCV2026. More modifications may be performed
summary: Aerial-Ground Person Re-IDentification (AG-ReID) aims to retrieve the same person across heterogeneous aerial and ground camera platforms. Although great progress has been made, existing methods remain suboptimal due to the direct feature alignment across views, overlooking view-specific cues. To address this issue, we propose a novel Hierarchical Hyperbolic Representation (HiHR) framework for AG-ReID. More specifically, we first extract multi-granularity features based on pre-trained visual-text encoders. Then, we propose a Text-guided Multi-granularity Fusion (TMF) to fuse multi-granularity features and enhance the representation ability of identity features. Furthermore, we introduce the Hierarchical Hyperbolic Learning (HHL) to construct a hierarchical feature structure in a hyperbolic space. This hierarchy includes a coarse level that ensures identity separability and cross-view consistency, and a fine level that preserves view-specific discriminative cues. As a result, our proposed framework can effectively aggregate view-invariant and view-specific discriminative features for AG-ReID. Extensive experiments on four AG-ReID benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework. The source code is available at https://github.com/YangQiWei3/HiHR.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Hierarchical Hyperbolic Representation (HiHR) framework for Aerial-Ground Person Re-ID (AG-ReID) that uses text-guided multi-granularity fusion and hierarchical hyperbolic learning to jointly capture view-invariant and view-specific features, outperforming existing methods on four benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing AG-ReID methods are suboptimal because they directly align features across aerial and ground views, overlooking view-specific cues that are important for discriminative person re-identification.
AI.method: The HiHR framework consists of: (1) multi-granularity feature extraction using pre-trained visual-text encoders; (2) Text-guided Multi-granularity Fusion (TMF) to fuse features across granularities; (3) Hierarchical Hyperbolic Learning (HHL) that constructs a coarse level for identity separability and cross-view consistency, and a fine level for preserving view-specific discriminative cues in hyperbolic space.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on four AG-ReID benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
AI.conclusion: The hierarchical hyperbolic representation enables effective aggregation of both view-invariant and view-specific discriminative features, addressing the limitations of direct cross-view feature alignment in AG-ReID.

title: Pitfalls and Remedies for Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization
summary: Bayesian optimization routinely warm-starts a target experiment with data from related source tasks, and the multi-task Gaussian process is the textbook surrogate for the job. We revisit this default in a controlled setting and find that it misestimates the cross-task correlation even in the simplest non-trivial case, affinely related source and target tasks, where a working transfer learning method should obviously succeed. We trace the failure to two independent structural mechanisms. Per-task standardization, the textbook fix for the affine slice ambiguity, propagates a finite-sample alignment error into the recovered correlation. The marginal likelihood itself identifies the correlation only at a per-sample rate that a Gaussian process at non-overlapping designs further dilutes. We propose three conservative remedies that follow from the analysis: promoting per-task means and scales to model parameters, restricting the task covariance to non-negative correlations, and co-locating part of the source and target designs. Across synthetic multi-task problems and surrogate-based hyperparameter tuning transfer, these remedies recover the target-only baseline on the simple instances, while the broader failure persists on harder instances and across most rank-based and latent-context variants.

AI.tldr: Bayesian optimization's default multi-task Gaussian process surrogate misestimates cross-task correlation even in simple affinely related source-target settings due to two structural failures: per-task standardization propagating alignment errors, and marginal likelihood identifying correlation at a per-sample rate diluted by non-overlapping designs. Three conservative remedies (promoting per-task parameters, restricting to non-negative correlations, co-locating designs) recover baseline performance on simple cases but fail on harder instances.
AI.motivation: To critically evaluate and improve the default multi-task Gaussian process surrogate used for warm-starting Bayesian optimization, since it fails even in the simplest non-trivial transfer learning scenario (affinely related tasks).
AI.method: Controlled empirical analysis tracing failure to two structural mechanisms: (1) per-task standardization propagating finite-sample alignment error into correlation recovery, and (2) marginal likelihood identifying correlation at a per-sample rate diluted by non-overlapping designs. Proposes three remedies: promoting per-task means/scales to model parameters, restricting task covariance to non-negative correlations, and co-locating source/target designs. Tested on synthetic multi-task problems and surrogate-based hyperparameter tuning transfer.
AI.result: The three proposed remedies recover the target-only baseline on simple affinely related instances, but the broader failure persists on harder instances and across most rank-based and latent-context variants.
AI.conclusion: The default multi-task GP surrogate has fundamental structural flaws in estimating cross-task correlation even under simple affine relationships. While conservative fixes help in simple cases, the problem remains unsolved for harder transfer learning scenarios.

title: YeTI: You Only Need Two Noisy Images for Real-World sRGB Noise Generation
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. Includes supplementary material
summary: Real-world sRGB image denoising remains challenging due to the nonlinear characteristics of sensor noise and the difficulty of acquiring aligned clean-noisy image pairs. Supervised denoisers often overfit to limited paired datasets, while self-supervised methods still depend on sufficiently diverse noisy observations. These limitations motivate scalable noise synthesis methods that can model real-world noise without clean ground truth or camera metadata. We propose YeTI, a real-world sRGB noise generation framework that learns from only two noisy observations of the same scene. YeTI uses a Reconstruction Autoencoder to disentangle scene structure and noise characteristics, and models the latent noise distribution with a one-step Conditional Diffusion Transformer trained using consistency objectives. Given a single noisy input at inference time, YeTI generates realistic, signal-dependent noise while preserving the underlying scene content. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of YeTI across real-world benchmarks. We evaluate noise generation on SIDD and further assess generalization on SIDD+, MAI2021, and SID, covering smartphone and diverse consumer-camera sensors. Downstream denoising results on DND further show that denoisers trained with YeTI-synthesized images achieve strong real-world performance, highlighting the practical value of clean-image-free and metadata-free noise generation.

AI.tldr: YeTI is a real-world sRGB noise generation framework that learns from only two noisy observations of the same scene. It uses a Reconstruction Autoencoder to disentangle scene structure from noise and a one-step Conditional Diffusion Transformer to model noise distribution. At inference, it generates realistic signal-dependent noise from a single noisy input without requiring clean images or camera metadata, achieving strong performance across benchmarks and downstream denoising tasks.
AI.motivation: Real-world sRGB image denoising is challenging due to nonlinear sensor noise characteristics and the difficulty of obtaining aligned clean-noisy image pairs. Supervised methods overfit to limited paired data, and self-supervised methods require diverse noisy observations, motivating a scalable noise synthesis approach that works without clean ground truth or camera metadata.
AI.method: YeTI comprises a Reconstruction Autoencoder that disentangles scene structure and noise characteristics from only two noisy observations, and a one-step Conditional Diffusion Transformer trained via consistency objectives to model the latent noise distribution. At inference, it generates realistic signal-dependent noise from a single noisy input.
AI.result: YeTI achieves effective noise generation on SIDD and generalizes well to SIDD+, MAI2021, and SID across smartphone and consumer-camera sensors. Downstream denoisers trained with YeTI-synthesized images achieve strong real-world performance on DND.
AI.conclusion: YeTI demonstrates that clean-image-free and metadata-free noise generation is practically viable for real-world sRGB denoising, highlighting the practical value of the proposed approach.

title: A Survey on the Green Development of Large Models: From Resource-Efficient Architectures to Hardware-Software Co-Design
comment: This paper has been accepted by CJE (2026), paper homepage: https://cje.ejournal.org.cn/article/doi/10.23919/cje.2025.00.438
summary: The rapid expansion of large-scale AI models has led to significant performance breakthroughs across diverse domains, yet it has also raised critical concerns regarding computational costs, energy consumption, and environmental sustainability. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the green development of large models, emphasizing resource-efficient architectures and full-stack hardware-software co-design. We systematically review recent advances in efficient model construction, including attention operator optimization, linear-complexity architectures, and model sparsification and merging, as well as training and deployment strategies such as data-efficient learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and computational compression. Beyond algorithmic improvements, we explore energy-efficient AI hardware, including mainstream AI chips, memory optimization, cross-platform deployment, and sustainable infrastructure. Furthermore, we examine how large models are being applied to sustainability-critical domains such as DeepSeek, remote sensing interpretation, national-scale infrastructure, and global initiatives. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, highlighting the need for continual learning paradigms, memory-centric hardware, and standardized evaluation protocols. This survey aims to offer a holistic roadmap toward sustainable, scalable, and socially responsible development of large models. Paper homepage: https://cje.ejournal.org.cn/article/doi/10.23919/cje.2025.00.438

AI.tldr: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of green development for large-scale AI models, covering efficient architectures (attention optimization, linear-complexity models, sparsification), training strategies (data-efficient learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, compression), energy-efficient hardware (AI chips, memory optimization, cross-platform deployment), and applications in sustainability domains (DeepSeek, remote sensing, infrastructure). It also discusses challenges and future directions toward sustainable and responsible AI.
AI.motivation: Rapid expansion of large-scale AI models has led to significant performance breakthroughs but also raised critical concerns regarding computational costs, energy consumption, and environmental sustainability.
AI.method: The survey systematically reviews efficient model construction (attention operator optimization, linear-complexity architectures, model sparsification and merging), training/deployment strategies (data-efficient learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, computational compression), and energy-efficient AI hardware (mainstream AI chips, memory optimization, cross-platform deployment, sustainable infrastructure).
AI.result: A comprehensive overview of green development strategies for large models, including efficient architectures, hardware-software co-design, and applications in sustainability-critical domains such as DeepSeek, remote sensing, and national-scale infrastructure.
AI.conclusion: Key challenges and future directions include continual learning paradigms, memory-centric hardware, and standardized evaluation protocols. The survey offers a holistic roadmap toward sustainable, scalable, and socially responsible development of large models.

title: Glob3R: Global Structure-from-Motion with 3D Foundation Models
summary: Recent 3D geometric foundation models, such as VGGT, provide robust feed-forward 3D reconstruction by directly predicting camera poses and 3D scene points from input images. However, their results remain inaccurate, and scaling them to long sequences or large unordered image sets typically requires chunk-wise processing, which can introduce drift and inconsistency. We present Glob3R, a global SfM-style reconstruction built on 3D foundation models. Our key idea is to explicitly optimize feed-forward geometric predictions. To this end, we augment a frozen Pi3X backbone with a lightweight dense matching head that predicts image warps between selected reference frames and neighboring views. These dense warps are converted into sparse but reliable multi-view feature tracks, which provide correspondence constraints for global optimization. We further introduce a keyframe-based sliding-window association strategy that propagates tracks and relative poses across overlapping windows, enabling scalable reconstruction. Finally, we perform global motion averaging and bundle adjustment to refine camera poses, reduce scale inconsistencies, and recover dense scene geometry. Extensive experiments on indoor, outdoor, large-scale driving, and unordered SfM benchmarks demonstrate that Glob3R achieves robust and accurate reconstruction. It consistently improves over feed-forward foundation-model baselines and recent scalable reconstruction methods, while being more robust than classical SfM pipelines. The refined poses also lead to higher-quality neural rendering, validating the benefit of combining foundation-model priors with global geometric optimization. Project page: https://junyuandeng.github.io/Glob3r

AI.tldr: Glob3R is a global SfM-style reconstruction method that augments a frozen 3D foundation model (Pi3X) with a dense matching head and sliding-window association to explicitly optimize feed-forward geometric predictions via global motion averaging and bundle adjustment, achieving robust and accurate 3D reconstruction across diverse benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D geometric foundation models (e.g., VGGT) provide fast feed-forward 3D reconstruction but suffer from inaccuracies and drift when scaled to long sequences or large unordered image sets due to chunk-wise processing.
AI.method: Augments a frozen Pi3X backbone with a lightweight dense matching head for predicting image warps between reference and neighboring views; converts dense warps into sparse multi-view feature tracks; uses keyframe-based sliding-window association to propagate tracks and relative poses across overlapping windows; performs global motion averaging and bundle adjustment to refine camera poses and recover dense scene geometry.
AI.result: Outperforms feed-forward foundation-model baselines and recent scalable reconstruction methods on indoor, outdoor, large-scale driving, and unordered SfM benchmarks; refined poses also improve neural rendering quality.
AI.conclusion: Combining foundation-model priors with explicit global geometric optimization yields more robust and accurate reconstruction than either feed-forward methods or classical SfM pipelines alone.

title: EXHOLD: Experience-Aware Real-Time Hold Control for Large-Scale Ride-Hailing Matching at DiDi
summary:
In large-scale ride-hailing, hold control is a critical mechanism for improving passenger-driver experience. By selectively delaying certain driver-order pairs, the system waits for better opportunities, reduces cancellations, and mitigates wasted driver effort. However, existing industrial hold strategies often rely on heuristic thresholding over multiple predictive models, which can be brittle under non-stationary traffic and hard to optimize for multi-objective experience signals.
  We propose EXHOLD, a deployable two-stage framework decoupling experience-aware pair assessment from hold-time execution. In Stage I, we learn a decision model assigning each driver-order pair to discrete, interpretable experience tiers by optimizing a unified objective that aggregates satisfaction signals across the matching funnel. In Stage II, we solve for a monotone hold-time schedule via constrained optimization over empirical quantiles. This explicitly enforces service guardrails bounding the unnecessary holding of promising matches while maximizing overall experience improvement.
  We evaluate EXHOLD through randomized A/B experiments in DiDi's production system in Brazil. Results show consistent gains in marketplace efficiency and experience: EXHOLD increases trip completion and driver income, significantly reduces passenger cancellations, and improves funnel efficiency. Ablations and behavioral analyses confirm both stages are essential and that the policy makes calibrated decisions under spatiotemporal heterogeneity. EXHOLD is currently deployed, serving production traffic in Brazil.

AI.tldr: EXHOLD is a two-stage hold control framework for ride-hailing that decouples experience-aware pair assessment from hold-time execution, achieving consistent improvements in marketplace efficiency and experience in DiDi's production system in Brazil through randomized A/B experiments.
AI.motivation: Existing industrial hold strategies rely on heuristic thresholding over multiple predictive models, which are brittle under non-stationary traffic and hard to optimize for multi-objective experience signals.
AI.method: A two-stage framework: Stage I learns a decision model assigning driver-order pairs to discrete experience tiers via unified optimization; Stage II solves for a monotone hold-time schedule via constrained optimization over empirical quantiles with service guardrails.
AI.result: Randomized A/B experiments in DiDi's production system in Brazil show consistent gains in trip completion, driver income, reduced passenger cancellations, and improved funnel efficiency. Both stages are essential and policy makes calibrated decisions under spatiotemporal heterogeneity.
AI.conclusion: EXHOLD is a deployable, effective hold control framework currently serving production traffic in Brazil, demonstrating robust improvements over heuristic thresholding approaches.

title: AnythingReality: Robust Online Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Open-Vocabulary VR Scene Exploration
summary: We present a novel integrated architecture for robust online 3D Gaussian splatting, real-time VR exploration, and speech-driven Vision-Language-Model interaction. Unlike methods assuming clean depth or external poses, our system combines ORB-SLAM3-based pose estimation with online Gaussian reconstruction for noisy real-world data. A VR pipeline enables immersive exploration of incremental reconstructions; a semantic module transcribes voice commands, generates scene descriptions, and records points of interest. Against state-of-the-art online Gaussian splatting methods, we improve image quality on our dataset (+14.5% PSNR, +8.6% SSIM, -14.3% LPIPS) and TUM-RGBD (+11.7% PSNR, +7.8% SSIM, -21.6% LPIPS), with comparable or superior frame rates via quality-speed configurations. We achieve an 88% VLM object-recognition rate.

AI.tldr: A novel system integrating ORB-SLAM3-based online 3D Gaussian splatting, VR exploration, and speech-driven VLM interaction, achieving superior image quality and 88% VLM recognition rate.
AI.motivation: Existing online Gaussian splatting methods assume clean depth or external poses, failing on noisy real-world data; there is also a lack of integrated pipelines combining reconstruction, VR exploration, and semantic interaction.
AI.method: The system combines ORB-SLAM3 for pose estimation with online 3D Gaussian splatting for robust reconstruction from noisy data, a VR pipeline for immersive exploration, and a semantic module for speech transcription, scene description, and point-of-interest recording.
AI.result: Outperforms SOTA online Gaussian splatting: +14.5% PSNR, +8.6% SSIM, -14.3% LPIPS on their dataset; +11.7% PSNR, +7.8% SSIM, -21.6% LPIPS on TUM-RGBD; 88% VLM object-recognition rate.
AI.conclusion: The integrated architecture demonstrates robust real-time reconstruction and interactive VR-VLM capabilities, with quality-speed trade-off configurations delivering comparable or superior frame rates.

title: Quantum Circuits in Diffusion Models: A Fair-Comparison Study and a Mechanistic Analysis of Angle-Embedding Failures
summary: We study the integration of variational quantum circuits (VQCs) into diffusion models through a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) channel-modulation scaffold that isolates the quantum contribution. Using a role-matched classical control and multi-seed significance testing across DDPM and latent diffusion on MNIST and CIFAR-10, with a score-based NCSN study on MNIST, we find that quantum cores achieve comparable mean FID to the classical control across DDPM and latent diffusion, while paired sampling-seed tests for EfficientSU2 detect no statistically significant difference. Although the quantum cores use $4.5$--$9\times$ fewer core parameters than the role-matched control, parameter-matched classical controls attain comparable mean FID, so the experiments do not establish a quantum parameter-efficiency advantage. We further identify a structural failure in score-based NCSN: the unbounded score target, proportional to $1/σ$, drives angle-embedding inputs far beyond the $2π$ period of rotation gates, causing phase aliasing and collapse of the quantum modulator. A bounding transformation, $θ\leftarrow π\tanh(\cdot)$, maps inputs to the non-aliasing domain and substantially improves both quantum cores. Since all circuits are classically simulated at a few-qubit scale, we do not claim quantum advantage. Instead, the study provides a fair-comparison protocol for quantum-enhanced generative models and a mechanistic account of when and why angle embeddings fail.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates variational quantum circuits integrated into diffusion models via a squeeze-and-excitation channel-modulation framework. Quantum cores achieve comparable FID to classical controls with fewer parameters, but parameter-matched classical controls perform similarly, yielding no evidence of quantum parameter-efficiency advantage. The study identifies a structural failure in score-based NCSN due to unbounded score targets causing phase aliasing, and proposes a bounding transformation to mitigate this issue. No quantum advantage is claimed.
AI.motivation: To fairly evaluate whether variational quantum circuits can enhance diffusion models (DDPM, latent diffusion, score-based NCSN) and to establish a rigorous comparative protocol that avoids common pitfalls in quantum-classical benchmarking.
AI.method: Integrates VQCs into diffusion models via an SE channel-modulation scaffold that isolates quantum contributions. Uses role-matched and parameter-matched classical controls, multi-seed significance testing, and paired sampling-seed statistical tests. Investigates DDPM and latent diffusion on MNIST/CIFAR-10, and score-based NCSN on MNIST. Identifies phase aliasing failure in NCSN and applies a bounding transformation (θ ← π tanh(·)).
AI.result: Quantum cores achieve comparable mean FID to classical controls in DDPM and latent diffusion; paired tests show no statistically significant difference for EfficientSU2. Quantum cores use 4.5–9× fewer core parameters, but parameter-matched classical controls achieve comparable FID, so no quantum parameter-efficiency advantage is established. Score-based NCSN suffers structural failure due to unbounded score targets causing phase aliasing; the bounding transformation substantially improves quantum cores.
AI.conclusion: No quantum advantage is observed; the paper provides a fair-comparison protocol for quantum-enhanced generative models and a mechanistic explanation of angle-embedding failures in score-based models.

title: Semantic Hardness Is Not Visual Hardness: Sign-Aware Hard Negative Mining for Sign Language Retrieval
summary: Sign Language Retrieval (SLRet) enables efficient access to sign language content but remains fragile in fine-grained scenarios where visually similar signs must be distinguished. We show that this limitation does not stem from model capacity, but from ineffective hard negative supervision. Specifically, we formulate fine-grained retrieval failures as a negative distribution mismatch: semantically distinct yet visually confusable signs are rarely treated as hard negatives, while existing text-based mining strategies fail to capture such visual ambiguity. To address this issue, we propose Sign-Aware Hard Negative Mining (SAN), which constructs hard negatives based on visual confusability in the sign embedding space rather than linguistic similarity. Experiments on PHOENIX-2014T demonstrate that SAN substantially improves fine-grained retrieval performance while preserving coarse-grained accuracy, highlighting the importance of aligning negative supervision with visual ambiguity in sign language retrieval.

AI.tldr: SAN improves fine-grained sign language retrieval by mining hard negatives based on visual confusability rather than linguistic similarity, addressing the negative distribution mismatch problem.
AI.motivation: Fine-grained sign language retrieval fails because semantically distinct but visually confusable signs are rarely treated as hard negatives; existing text-based mining strategies cannot capture visual ambiguity.
AI.method: Proposes Sign-Aware Hard Negative Mining (SAN), which constructs hard negatives based on visual confusability in the sign embedding space instead of linguistic similarity.
AI.result: On PHOENIX-2014T, SAN substantially improves fine-grained retrieval while preserving coarse-grained accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Aligning negative supervision with visual ambiguity is crucial for sign language retrieval; the bottleneck is not model capacity but ineffective hard negative supervision.

title: Power Flow Feasibility Assessment Using Variational Graph Autoencoders
summary: Data-driven methods, including graph neural networks, have been studied for accelerating power flow calculations in recent years, but very little attention has been paid to the solution feasibility, which can be obtained by traditional solvers. This paper presents a Variational Graph Autoencoder (VGAE) that detects the power flow solution feasibility, using the IEEE 118-bus case, to assess the validity of the solutions provided by AI-driven solvers.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Variational Graph Autoencoder (VGAE) approach using the IEEE 118-bus case to detect power flow solution feasibility, addressing the lack of attention to feasibility verification in AI-driven power flow solvers.
AI.motivation: Current data-driven methods for power flow calculations largely neglect solution feasibility verification, which traditional solvers can provide. The authors aim to bridge this gap by developing a method to assess the validity of AI-driven power flow solutions.
AI.method: The authors employ a Variational Graph Autoencoder (VGAE) model trained on the IEEE 118-bus system to detect whether power flow solutions provided by AI-driven solvers are feasible.
AI.result: The VGAE model demonstrates capability in assessing the validity of solutions from AI-driven power flow solvers on the IEEE 118-bus test case.
AI.conclusion: VGAE-based feasibility detection offers a promising approach to verify solution validity in data-driven power flow calculations, addressing a critical gap in current research.

title: REMIND: RE-Identification with Memory for INDoor Navigation
summary:
Mobile robots operating indoors must re-identify previously observed objects after long temporal gaps, significant viewpoint changes, and severe illumination variations. This remains a challenging problem: multi-object tracking methods are optimized for short-term association of pedestrians and vehicles at video rates, person and vehicle re-identification approaches lack persistent memory mechanisms, and state-of-the-art video object segmentation techniques rely on reactive distractor filtering rather than enforcing global identity consistency.
  To address these limitations, we present REMIND, an online tracker designed for long-term multi-object re-identification of generic indoor objects from monocular RGB imagery, requiring neither camera pose nor depth. Motivated by evidence from visual cognition that humans rely on accumulated appearance familiarity and spatial context rather than explicit self-localization, REMIND combines frozen DINOv3 features with a dual-bank multi-prototype appearance memory, part- and background-level descriptors, a neighbour-context reasoning module exploiting spatial co-occurrence, and joint Hungarian assignment with ambiguity-aware safeguards. On a purpose-built indoor dataset featuring controlled revisits and dense same-class clutter, REMIND reaches 90.35% IDF1, nearly 20 points above a state-of-the-art video object segmentation baseline and more than 36 above a strong tracking-by-detection baseline. On ScanNet++, it attains the highest IDF1 in every setting but one, end-to-end detection over all scenes, where the tracking-by-detection baseline is marginally ahead while REMIND still associates and recovers identities more accurately; it also completes every scene, whereas the video object segmentation baseline exhausts GPU memory on 66.9% under YOLO detections. The complete system, evaluation framework, and dataset are publicly released.

AI.tldr: REMIND is an online tracker for long-term multi-object re-identification of generic indoor objects from monocular RGB video, achieving 90.35% IDF1 on a purpose-built dataset—20+ points above video object segmentation baselines—by combining frozen DINOv3 features, dual-bank multi-prototype appearance memory, spatial context reasoning, and ambiguity-aware Hungarian assignment.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-object tracking, re-identification, and video object segmentation methods fail at long-term object re-identification indoors due to reliance on short-term association, lack of persistent memory, or reactive distractor filtering without enforcing global identity consistency.
AI.method: REMIND combines frozen DINOv3 features, a dual-bank multi-prototype appearance memory, part- and background-level descriptors, a neighbour-context reasoning module exploiting spatial co-occurrence, and joint Hungarian assignment with ambiguity-aware safeguards. It operates online from monocular RGB, requiring no camera pose or depth.
AI.result: REMIND achieves 90.35% IDF1 on a purpose-built indoor dataset (≈20 points above video object segmentation baseline, >36 above tracking-by-detection). On ScanNet++, it attains highest IDF1 in all but one setting and runs fully on all scenes while the video object segmentation baseline exhausts GPU memory on 66.9% of scenes with YOLO detections.
AI.conclusion: The dual-bank memory with prototype-level appearance descriptors and spatial context reasoning enables robust long-term re-identification indoors. The system, framework, and dataset are publicly released.

title: Present but Rescaled: Chat-to-Agent Transfer of Additive Activation Steering
summary: Additive activation steering (injecting a scaled residual-stream direction during generation) is calibrated almost entirely in single-turn chat, yet the models it targets are increasingly deployed as tool-using ReAct agents. We present the first systematic chat-to-agent transfer study of additive steering, coupling behavioral measurement with a representation read-out in a matched-information design: the same items rendered as plain chat or as a ReAct tool-use episode, with matched-norm random-direction controls and the transcript re-encoded every turn to exclude KV-cache contamination. Transfer is real but rescaled, and the right description is a dissociation: the injected direction reaches the late layers at near-full strength in every setting and model tested (install-site agent-over-chat ratios 0.83-1.16 across three families), while the behavioral coupling is reset per model and context. On Qwen2.5-7B a refusal bypass vector amplifies in the agent (T = 1.45, CI [1.20, 1.78], N = 300); across a powered uniform-protocol distribution the coupling spans amplification (Gemma-2-9B T = 2.00) to attenuation (Yi-1.5-9B T = 0.43, CI [0.29, 0.60]), with no universal constant and a single clean attenuator against a universal sign. Directional ablation of the same axis does not amplify (T = 0.93, CI including 1) while additive injection amplifies (T = 1.50), a 20.1-point gain difference (CI [13.4, 26.8]) that identifies an additive-specific mechanism. Two pre-registered instruments converge to localize the rescaling to the ReAct format scaffold, before any tool observation, rather than to the observation boundary where a dilution account would predict it. The safety implication is immediate and unpredictable: agentic deployment amplifies steering-based refusal bypass by up to 2.00x on some models while others attenuate, so a deployment cannot assume a given model is safe under additive steering.

AI.tldr: Additive activation steering transfers from chat to ReAct agents but with a dissociation: the injected direction reaches late layers at near-full strength across settings, while behavioral coupling varies unpredictably per model and context (amplification up to 2.00x on some models, attenuation on others). This makes deployment safety assumptions unreliable under additive steering.
AI.motivation: Additive activation steering is calibrated on single-turn chat, but increasingly deployed on tool-using ReAct agents. There is no systematic understanding of how steering transfers from chat to agentic settings.
AI.method: Matched-information design comparing the same items as plain chat vs. ReAct episodes, with matched-norm random-direction controls, transcript re-encoding per turn to avoid KV-cache contamination, and both behavioral measurement and representation read-out across three model families.
AI.result: The injected direction reaches late layers at near-full strength in all settings (agent/chat ratios 0.83-1.16), but behavioral coupling varies widely: Qwen2.5-7B amplifies (T=1.45), Gemma-2-9B amplifies (T=2.00), Yi-1.5-9B attenuates (T=0.43). Directional ablation does not amplify (T=0.93) while injection does (T=1.50), a 20.1-point gain difference. The rescaling localizes to the ReAct format scaffold before tool observation.
AI.conclusion: Agentic deployment amplifies steering-based refusal bypass up to 2.00x on some models while others attenuate; deployment cannot assume a given model is safe under additive steering. The effect is additive-specific and originates from the ReAct format scaffold.

title: Rethinking Monocular Depth Embedding for Generalized Stereo Matching
summary: Generally, monocular methods capture rich contextual priors but lack geometric precision, whereas stereo methods are geometrically accurate yet struggle in textureless and occluded regions. Several approaches attempt to combine their strengths to enhance the generalization of stereo matching (SM) by aligning monocular depth with stereo information. However, establishing a stable and generalizable alignment is challenging, and unreliable monocular cues can substantially degrade performance. This paper rethinks monocular depth embedding. First, to prevent shortcut learning, we reduce branch coupling instead of expanding network width. Second, we construct soft constraints instead of hard ones from monocular depth to improve tolerance to monocular depth errors. Based on the principles, we integrate monocular information into both feature extraction and GRU iterations. Specifically, the monocular depth map is fused with the RGB image to sharpen depth boundary perception and suppress matching ambiguities. The fused image is then used for feature extraction, allowing the contextual features to encode global geometric information. Furthermore, the monocular depth gradient feature is employed to guide disparity updates, helping to escape local oscillations. Finally, to address the boundary blurring of supervised disparity caused by data augmentation, we propose an edge confidence estimation method and an edge-aware loss function. Our method achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on multiple standard benchmarks, demonstrating excellent generalization while improving accuracy. The code is available at https://github.com/linliboabc-maker/stereo-matching-digital.

AI.tldr: A novel stereo matching method that integrates monocular depth cues via soft constraints and reduced branch coupling, achieving SOTA generalization and accuracy on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Monocular methods have rich context but lack geometric precision, while stereo methods are geometrically accurate but struggle in textureless/occluded regions. Existing hybrid approaches suffer from unreliable monocular cues degrading performance. The paper aims to achieve stable, generalizable integration of monocular depth into stereo matching.
AI.method: (1) Reduces branch coupling (instead of expanding network width) to prevent shortcut learning. (2) Constructs soft constraints from monocular depth to tolerate depth errors. (3) Fuses monocular depth with RGB to sharpen boundary perception and suppress matching ambiguities. (4) Uses monocular depth gradient features to guide GRU-based disparity updates, avoiding local oscillations. (5) Proposes edge confidence estimation and edge-aware loss to address boundary blurring from data augmentation.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on multiple standard benchmarks with excellent generalization and improved accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Rethinking monocular depth embedding via soft constraints and reduced coupling enables robust stereo matching that generalizes well, outperforming prior methods.

title: A Personalized Computational Framework for Assessing the Sufficiency of Partially Observed Data in Healthcare AI models
summary: Achieving early and timely diagnosis and treatment for disease is a major challenge. Recent applications of machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on patient data have shown promise in many different settings for predicting the patient health state. A challenge often faced when applying these ML algorithms is that at any given time, not all clinical variables (features) needed as input to perform prediction tasks are available. We define the concept of full-feature-capacity (FFC) to refer to prediction performance when such algorithms make use of all features on which they were trained. We then introduce Feature Sufficiency Analysis (FSA) - an analysis for determining whether a subset of all clinical features needed by an AI model is sufficient to achieve FFC. FSA estimates the underlying distributions of missing variables conditioned on features that are available. FSA provides a patient-specific assessment of whether the existing set of measured features achieves FFC. If yes, then there is no need to acquire further inputs and a ML-based prediction. We provide two case studies: prediction of need for postoperative prolonged ventilation in patients recovering from heart surgery; 10-year mortality prediction in an outpatient cohort. We also demonstrate that FSA also provides a clinically interpretable feature-ranking methodology based on prediction sufficiency, identifies intrinsically hard-to-predict patient populations, and has the potential to perform cost-aware optimization for clinical data acquisition. FSA provides a generic computational approach for determining whether incomplete clinical information is sufficient to support trustworthy AI-assisted clinical decision-making, thereby facilitating the prospective deployment of healthcare AI systems across diverse clinical settings.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Feature Sufficiency Analysis (FSA) to determine if a subset of available clinical features is sufficient to achieve full-feature-capacity (FFC) prediction performance, enabling trustworthy AI-assisted clinical decision-making with incomplete data.
AI.motivation: ML algorithms for disease prediction often require complete clinical feature sets, but in practice not all features are available at any given time, hindering deployment of healthcare AI systems.
AI.method: FSA estimates underlying distributions of missing variables conditioned on available features and provides patient-specific assessment of whether the existing measured features achieve FFC performance.
AI.result: Demonstrated on two case studies: predicting postoperative prolonged ventilation after heart surgery and 10-year mortality prediction in an outpatient cohort. FSA also provides clinically interpretable feature-ranking, identifies hard-to-predict populations, and enables cost-aware optimization for data acquisition.
AI.conclusion: FSA is a generic computational approach for determining whether incomplete clinical information is sufficient for trustworthy AI-assisted clinical decision-making, facilitating prospective deployment of healthcare AI systems across diverse clinical settings.

title: TextileNet: Towards Zero-shot Text-style Segmentation of Manuscripts
comment: accepted for publication in the ICDAR 2026 workshop (peer reviewed) "IWCP: 4th International Workshop on Computational Paleography"
summary: Automatic writer identification systems have progressed remarkably in recent years, yet their deployment in archival paleography remains limited by the scarcity of labeled training data, open scribe sets, and degraded image quality. We present TextileNet, a fully convolutional multi-task network trained exclusively on synthetic data to produce dense pixel-level texture embeddings, which we transfer zeroshot to historical manuscript analysis. As an original contribution to evaluation methodology, we designed a paleographic visual quiz of 80 pair and triplet questions and administered it to a range from lay participants to senior paleographers under strict anonymity, establishing to our knowledge for the first time a human baseline for script-style discrimination on late medieval text. We employ TextileNet embeddings to perform zero-shot retrieval on sub-word granularity for hand and gender identification. Our experimental results help in building the credibility of TextileNet in the paleographic domain, but more than that demonstrate in experimental terms that the question of gender in handwriting needs to be treated with caution.

AI.tldr: TextileNet is a fully convolutional multi-task network trained on synthetic data to produce dense pixel-level texture embeddings for zero-shot historical manuscript analysis, achieving credible results in paleographic tasks while revealing caution is needed regarding gender identification in handwriting.
AI.motivation: Automatic writer identification has progressed but remains limited in archival paleography due to scarce labeled data, open scribe sets, and degraded image quality. The paper aims to overcome these challenges with a zero-shot approach.
AI.method: TextileNet: a fully convolutional multi-task network trained exclusively on synthetic data to produce dense pixel-level texture embeddings, transferred zero-shot to historical manuscripts. Also introduces a paleographic visual quiz (80 pair/triplet questions) administered to laypeople to senior paleographers to establish a human baseline for script-style discrimination.
AI.result: TextileNet embeddings enable zero-shot retrieval at sub-word granularity for hand and gender identification. Results build credibility in the paleographic domain but demonstrate experimentally that gender in handwriting should be treated with caution.
AI.conclusion: TextileNet is credible for paleographic analysis via zero-shot transfer from synthetic data, but gender identification from handwriting is not reliably supported by experimental evidence.

title: COAST: Context-Aware Differential Learning for Gene Expression Prediction in Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Spatial transcriptomics enables profiling of spatial gene expression but is limited by high cost and low throughput, motivating prediction from H&E histopathology images. Existing context-aware methods mainly supervise absolute expression, while relative expression relationships between spots are rarely used explicitly. We propose COAST, a context-aware differential learning framework for spatial gene expression prediction. COAST conditions the local and global context features with type-specific modulation and aggregates the target and context spot tokens using a Transformer encoder to capture both fine-grained local patterns and slide-level structure. It is trained with a joint objective that combines absolute expression regression with signed differential regression between the target and context spots. Experiments on multiple spatial transcriptomics datasets show consistent improvements in correlation- and distribution-based metrics, demonstrating the effectiveness of context-aware differential learning for histology-based spatial gene expression prediction.

AI.tldr: COAST is a context-aware differential learning framework that predicts spatial gene expression from H&E histopathology images by combining absolute expression regression with signed differential regression between target and context spots, achieving consistent improvements across multiple spatial transcriptomics datasets.
AI.motivation: Spatial transcriptomics is limited by high cost and low throughput, motivating the need for cost-effective prediction from H&E histopathology images. Existing context-aware methods mainly supervise absolute expression and rarely utilize relative expression relationships between spots explicitly.
AI.method: COAST uses type-specific modulation to condition local and global context features, aggregates target and context spot tokens via a Transformer encoder for fine-grained local patterns and slide-level structure, and is trained with a joint objective combining absolute expression regression and signed differential regression between target and context spots.
AI.result: Consistent improvements in correlation- and distribution-based metrics across multiple spatial transcriptomics datasets.
AI.conclusion: Context-aware differential learning is effective for histology-based spatial gene expression prediction.

title: From Classification to Localization and Clinical Validation: Large-Scale Development of a Deep Learning System for Thoracic Disease Detection on Chest Radiographs in Thailand
summary: Chest radiography (CXR) remains the most widely used thoracic imaging modality, yet expert interpretation is constrained by a severe shortage of radiologists in Thailand and across Southeast Asia. Local adaptation of deep learning models to Thai data has been shown to substantially improve accuracy on Thai populations. Here we present the development and comprehensive validation of the chest radiograph analysis model in Inspectra CXR version 5, a deep learning system that performs multi-label thoracic disease classification and weakly supervised lesion localization within a single model. The architecture couples a DenseNet-121 backbone with Attend-and-Compare Modules (ACM) and a Probabilistic Class Activation Map (PCAM) aggregation layer, producing a per-condition classification score and heatmap simultaneously. The model was developed on 874,858 frontal chest radiographs with paired radiologist reports from Siriraj Hospital, Bangkok. On a held-out, radiologist-verified in-domain test set of 19,871 cases, it achieved a mean AUROC of 0.994 (mean sensitivity 92.4%, specificity 98.6%) across nine clinically important conditions. On an independent generalization set of 5,992 cases from 13 hospitals across Thailand, the mean AUROC was 0.970, indicating robust transfer across sites. For localization, evaluated on 4,549 radiologist-annotated cases, the model attained a mean lesion-localization fraction (LLF) of 77.9% at 0.59 non-lesion localizations per image. In a usability evaluation with five thoracic radiologists, the system reached a classification concordance of 93.6%, a localization concordance of 94.7%, and a mean System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 89. These results indicate that a locally developed, localization-capable CXR system can deliver high accuracy, generalize across heterogeneous Thai hospitals, and earn the trust of practicing radiologists.

AI.tldr: The authors present Inspectra CXR version 5, a deep learning system combining DenseNet-121 with Attend-and-Compare Modules (ACM) and Probabilistic Class Activation Map (PCAM) for multi-label thoracic disease classification and weakly supervised lesion localization. Trained on 874,858 frontal CXRs from Siriraj Hospital, Bangkok, it achieved a mean AUROC of 0.994 on in-domain test set and 0.970 across 13 Thai hospitals, with strong localization performance (LLF 77.9%) and high radiologist acceptance (SUS 89).
AI.motivation: Severe shortage of radiologists in Thailand and Southeast Asia limits expert CXR interpretation; locally adapted deep learning models improve accuracy on Thai populations, motivating development of a single-model system for both classification and localization.
AI.method: A DenseNet-121 backbone coupled with Attend-and-Compare Modules (ACM) and a Probabilistic Class Activation Map (PCAM) aggregation layer, enabling simultaneous multi-label thoracic disease classification and weakly supervised lesion localization. Trained on 874,858 frontal CXRs with paired radiologist reports.
AI.result: In-domain: mean AUROC 0.994 (sensitivity 92.4%, specificity 98.6%) on 19,871 cases. Generalization: mean AUROC 0.970 on 5,992 cases from 13 hospitals. Localization: LLF 77.9% at 0.59 false positives/image on 4,549 annotated cases. Usability: classification concordance 93.6%, localization concordance 94.7%, SUS score 89.
AI.conclusion: A locally developed, localization-capable CXR AI system can achieve high accuracy, generalize across heterogeneous hospitals in Thailand, and gain trust from practicing radiologists.

title: Understanding Schedule-Free Methods in Nonconvex Optimization: Rate Guarantees and Escaping Saddles
summary: Schedule-Free methods have attracted growing interest for alleviating the burden of designing and tuning a learning rate scheduler, while matching and sometimes even outperforming optimizers with tuned schedulers. Despite their strong empirical results, their convergence theory in nonconvex optimization, where modern machine learning objectives typically arise, has remained largely unexplored. In this paper, we provide worst-case analyses of Schedule-Free gradient descent and Schedule-Free stochastic gradient descent, in their standard form and without auxiliary modifications or restrictive conditions, for smooth but possibly nonconvex objectives. Based on a Lyapunov analysis derived from the continuous-time limiting ordinary differential equation associated with these methods, we show that Schedule-Free gradient descent and Schedule-Free stochastic gradient descent achieve the optimal worst-case convergence rates attainable among first-order methods. We further formulate Schedule-Free gradient descent as a nonautonomous dynamical system and prove strict-saddle avoidance under an arbitrarily small one-time perturbation. These theoretical results provide a better understanding of the strong performance that Schedule-Free methods demonstrate.

AI.tldr: This paper provides the first worst-case convergence analysis for Schedule-Free gradient descent and SGD in nonconvex smooth optimization, proving they achieve optimal first-order rates and avoid strict saddle points, matching their strong empirical performance.
AI.motivation: Schedule-Free methods have shown impressive empirical results matching or beating tuned schedulers, but their theoretical convergence guarantees in nonconvex optimization (common in modern ML) were missing. This paper aims to fill that gap.
AI.method: The authors use Lyapunov analysis derived from the continuous-time limiting ODE of Schedule-Free methods, and formulate Schedule-Free GD as a nonautonomous dynamical system to analyze strict-saddle avoidance under arbitrarily small one-time perturbations.
AI.result: Schedule-Free GD and SGD achieve optimal worst-case convergence rates among first-order methods for smooth nonconvex objectives. They also provably avoid strict saddle points with an arbitrarily small one-time perturbation.
AI.conclusion: The theoretical results explain and justify the strong empirical performance of Schedule-Free methods, confirming they are not just practically effective but also theoretically sound in nonconvex settings.

title: Application of machine learning to monster level prediction in tabletop RPG game design
summary: Designing balanced adversaries is a central but labor-intensive task in tabletop role-playing game (TTRPG) development. In systems such as Pathfinder, each monster is described by many numerical attributes that jointly determine its power, summarized as an ordinal level. We investigate whether machine learning can support designers by predicting this level from a monster's attributes, framing the task as tabular ordinal regression. We introduce what is, to our knowledge, the first dataset built specifically for TTRPG monster-level prediction, derived from publicly available Pathfinder Second Edition data. Using it, we compare classical regression models with rounding schemes, dedicated tabular ordinal regression algorithms, and neural networks with ordinal-aware losses. To mirror real design workflows, we evaluate all models under chronological and expanding-window protocols with several complementary metrics. Results show that tree-based ensembles outperform linear models and neural approaches, achieving near-perfect ordinal ranking and high predictive accuracy. Explainable AI analyses, such as feature importance and error distributions, show that the model is aligned with human intuition and follows patterns grounded in game rules. Together, these results show that machine learning can reliably approximate designer judgments and serve as an effective computer-aided tool for monster balancing and broader TTRPG system design.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the first dataset for TTRPG monster-level prediction from Pathfinder Second Edition, and compares classical regression, ordinal regression algorithms, and neural networks for predicting monster levels from attributes, finding tree-based ensembles achieve near-perfect ordinal ranking and high accuracy, with explanations aligned with human intuition and game rules.
AI.motivation: Designing balanced adversaries in TTRPGs like Pathfinder is labor-intensive, as each monster has many numerical attributes determining its power summarized as an ordinal level. The authors aim to investigate whether machine learning can support designers by predicting this level from attributes.
AI.method: Framed as tabular ordinal regression; introduced a new dataset from publicly available Pathfinder Second Edition data; compared classical regression with rounding schemes, dedicated tabular ordinal regression algorithms, and neural networks with ordinal-aware losses; evaluated under chronological and expanding-window protocols with multiple complementary metrics; used Explainable AI (feature importance, error distributions) for interpretation.
AI.result: Tree-based ensembles outperform linear models and neural approaches, achieving near-perfect ordinal ranking and high predictive accuracy. Explainable AI analyses show the model aligns with human intuition and follows patterns grounded in game rules.
AI.conclusion: Machine learning can reliably approximate designer judgments and serve as an effective computer-aided tool for monster balancing and broader TTRPG system design.

title: Simon-SR: Spatially Adaptive Modulation and Visual Prompt Adaptation for Text-Reinforced Super-Resolution
summary: Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) reconstructs high-quality images from low-resolution inputs. While recent multi-modal methods improve perceptual quality, they remain sensitive to erroneous priors and require expensive annotations. To address these issues, we propose Simon-SR, a multi-modal SISR framework leveraging learnable prompts for efficient semantic mining and robust text-image fusion. Our approach combines Contrastive Prompt Learning with Prompt-Guided Spatially Adaptive Refinement to enhance multi-modal alignment. Experiments demonstrate that Simon-SR surpasses state-of-the-art methods, achieving maximum improvements of 0.50 dB in PSNR, 0.0133 in SSIM, and 0.0695 in LPIPS. Code will be released.

AI.tldr: Simon-SR is a multi-modal SISR framework using learnable prompts for efficient semantic mining and robust text-image fusion, achieving state-of-the-art results with improvements of 0.50 dB PSNR, 0.0133 SSIM, and 0.0695 LPIPS.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-modal SISR methods suffer from sensitivity to erroneous priors and require expensive annotations. The authors aim to address these limitations by proposing a more robust and annotation-efficient framework.
AI.method: Simon-SR combines Contrastive Prompt Learning with Prompt-Guided Spatially Adaptive Refinement to enable efficient semantic mining and robust text-image fusion, leveraging learnable prompts instead of fixed or manually annotated priors.
AI.result: Simon-SR surpasses state-of-the-art methods, achieving maximum improvements of 0.50 dB in PSNR, 0.0133 in SSIM, and 0.0695 in LPIPS.
AI.conclusion: The proposed learnable prompt-based multi-modal fusion approach effectively improves SISR performance while reducing reliance on expensive annotations and mitigating sensitivity to erroneous priors.

title: Interference and Retention in Continual Learning
summary:
Continual learning commonly relies on post-hoc mechanisms such as replay, elastic regularization, or distillation. This work argues that forgetting should instead be modeled directly as interference between tasks. In the frozen-feature regime, forgetting from learning a new task is exactly the interference energy induced on the old task. In deep networks, the same quantity is recovered through path-averaged curvature with minimal additional forward passes.
  When task supports are disjoint, forgetting can be eliminated structurally and when task supports overlap in conflicting directions, a non-zero distortion floor is unavoidable. The same geometry optimally merges models through task-aware orthogonalization. From this analysis we derive Interference-Gated Functional Allocation (IGFA), a replay-free, Fisher-free method that shares directions when tasks align and protects them when they conflict. Across benchmarks, IGFA achieves lossless retention when tasks are structurally separable and moves unavoidable cost from irreversible forgetting into deferred but recoverable plasticity when they are not. It matches the strongest replay-free structural baselines on dissimilar-task streams and improves on unconditional projection when similarity makes transfer worth preserving.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes viewing continual learning forgetting as interference between tasks, deriving a replay-free, Fisher-free method called IGFA that protects or shares model directions based on task alignment, achieving lossless retention when tasks are separable and converting irreversible forgetting into recoverable plasticity otherwise.
AI.motivation: Current continual learning methods rely on post-hoc mechanisms (replay, regularization, distillation) rather than directly modeling forgetting. The authors argue forgetting should be modeled as interference between tasks to provide a more principled understanding of catastrophic forgetting.
AI.method: IGFA (Interference-Gated Functional Allocation) is a replay-free, Fisher-free method that: (1) models forgetting as interference energy in the frozen-feature regime, (2) uses path-averaged curvature to recover interference in deep networks, (3) shares model directions when tasks align and protects them when they conflict based on task geometry, and (4) applies task-aware orthogonalization for optimal model merging.
AI.result: IGFA achieves lossless retention when tasks are structurally separable, matches the strongest replay-free structural baselines on dissimilar-task streams, and improves on unconditional projection when similarity makes transfer worth preserving. It moves unavoidable cost from irreversible forgetting into deferred but recoverable plasticity when tasks conflict.
AI.conclusion: Forgetting is best understood as task interference; when task supports are disjoint forgetting can be eliminated structurally, and when they overlap in conflicting directions a non-zero distortion floor is unavoidable. IGFA demonstrates this geometric perspective yields practical benefits over existing continual learning approaches.

title: CtrlVTON: Controllable Virtual Try-On via Visual-Instance-Prompt Segmentation
summary: Virtual try-on (VTO) has made significant progress in realistically transferring garments onto a target person. Yet most systems give the user little control over how a garment should be worn -- its size (loose or fitted), style (e.g., tucked in or untucked, open or closed), and spatial placement on the body. We address this gap with two complementary contributions. First, we define and solve Visual-Instance-Prompt Segmentation via VIP-SAM: given a flatlay image of a garment, segment that specific instance in a photograph of a person wearing it. This is an instance-level task, distinct from the typically studied category-level segmentation. Second, we introduce CtrlVTON, a controllable VTO framework that recasts try-on as an image editing problem and adds segmentation masks as pixel-level control over garment layout, including style, size, and spatial placement on the body. VIP-SAM and CtrlVTON each achieve state-of-the-art results on their respective tasks. In particular, CtrlVTON generates images that follow user-provided layouts far more faithfully than the strongest proprietary editing systems while matching them on garment fidelity.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces VIP-SAM for instance-level garment segmentation and CtrlVTON for controllable virtual try-on, enabling precise control over garment size, style, and spatial placement. Both achieve state-of-the-art results.
AI.motivation: Existing VTO systems lack fine-grained user control over how a garment is worn (e.g., size, style, placement). The authors aim to address this gap by enabling pixel-level control over garment layout.
AI.method: Two contributions: (1) VIP-SAM for Visual-Instance-Prompt Segmentation, an instance-level segmentation task that segments a specific garment instance from a flatlay image in a photograph of a person wearing it. (2) CtrlVTON, a controllable VTO framework that treats try-on as an image editing problem and uses segmentation masks as pixel-level control signals for garment style, size, and spatial placement.
AI.result: VIP-SAM and CtrlVTON each achieve state-of-the-art results on their respective tasks. CtrlVTON generates images that follow user-provided layouts more faithfully than leading proprietary editing systems while matching them on garment fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The proposed methods significantly advance controllable virtual try-on by providing users with precise, pixel-level control over garment appearance and placement, outperforming existing systems in layout adherence while maintaining high garment fidelity.

title: Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting under Distribution Shifts: A Synthetic Evaluation
summary: Temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) represent evolving relational systems, whose underlying data-generating processes often change over time. Yet, TKG forecasting models are commonly evaluated only on empirical benchmark datasets that provide limited insight into the models' robustness to such distribution shifts. Recognising this issue, we study TKG forecasting under controlled shift environments using a synthetic TKG generator that encodes three temporal and structural properties -- recurrence, homophily, and periodicity -- as data-generating mechanisms. This allows us to evaluate seven forecasting architectures under stationary and shifting regimes. Our experiments suggest that robustness in TKG forecasting is highly signal-dependent. Recurrence-based and periodic regularities are largely recoverable under stationary conditions, and simple memory-based baselines can be competitive when recurrence dominates the data. However, structural breaks reveal limitations in model adaptivity, with shifts in latent entity-community structure posing the strongest challenge in our study. Overall, our findings improve the understanding of the capabilities and limitations of current TKG models confronted with temporal distribution shifts.

AI.tldr: This paper studies TKG forecasting under controlled distribution shifts using a synthetic data generator, finding that model robustness is signal-dependent: recurrence and periodicity are recoverable, but shifts in entity-community structure pose the greatest challenge.
AI.motivation: TKG forecasting models are typically evaluated on empirical benchmarks that do not reveal robustness to distribution shifts, which occur in real-world evolving relational systems.
AI.method: The authors use a synthetic TKG generator encoding three data-generating mechanisms (recurrence, homophily, periodicity) to evaluate seven forecasting architectures under stationary and shifting regimes.
AI.result: Recurrence-based and periodic regularities are largely recoverable in stationary conditions; simple memory-based baselines compete well when recurrence dominates. Structural breaks in latent entity-community structure severely challenge model adaptivity.
AI.conclusion: Robustness in TKG forecasting is highly signal-dependent, and structural shifts in community structure present the strongest challenge, highlighting limitations in current models' adaptivity.

title: SVF-CR: Synchronized Visual-Facial Cross-Refinement for Multimodal Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition
summary: Ambivalence and hesitancy are subtle behavioral states that are expressed through a combination of verbal content, facial behavior, visual context, and acoustic cues. Effective recognition therefore requires not only extracting informative unimodal representations, but also modeling how temporally aligned behavioral evidence interacts across modalities. In this paper, we propose a synchronized visual-facial cross-refinement framework (SVF-CR) with pairwise multimodal evidence fusion for ambivalence and hesitancy recognition. The proposed method first extracts whole-video segment tokens and cropped-face segment tokens using the same temporal partition. The synchronized visual and facial tokens are refined through intra-modal self-attention and bidirectional visual-facial cross-attention, allowing whole-video context and local facial behavior to mutually refine each other before evidence construction. We then construct segment-level visual-facial evidence using consistency and discrepancy modeling, followed by temporal self-attention and attention pooling. Textual and acoustic features are lightly refined through context self-attention and are fused with the enhanced visual-facial evidence at the final decision stage using pairwise evidence fusion. Experiments on the BAH (Behavioral Ambivalence/Hesitancy) public evaluation split show that the proposed synchronized visual-facial cross-refinement improves public macro-F1 over both global visual-face token fusion and synchronized evidence baselines, achieving a public macro-F1 of 0.7156. Code is available at : https://github.com/hiinnnii/BAH-Challenge-ECCV2026\_SVF-CR.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes SVF-CR, a synchronized visual-facial cross-refinement framework that uses cross-attention between whole-video and cropped-face tokens, along with pairwise multimodal evidence fusion, to recognize ambivalence and hesitancy from video, facial, textual, and acoustic cues. It achieves 0.7156 macro-F1 on the BAH dataset.
AI.motivation: Ambivalence and hesitancy are subtle behavioral states expressed through multiple modalities (verbal, facial, visual, acoustic), requiring not only informative unimodal representations but also modeling of temporally aligned cross-modal interactions, which existing methods lack.
AI.method: (1) Extract synchronized whole-video and cropped-face segment tokens via the same temporal partition; (2) Refine tokens through intra-modal self-attention and bidirectional visual-facial cross-attention; (3) Construct segment-level visual-facial evidence via consistency and discrepancy modeling; (4) Apply temporal self-attention and attention pooling; (5) Lightly refine textual and acoustic features via context self-attention; (6) Fuse all modalities at decision stage via pairwise evidence fusion.
AI.result: 0.7156 public macro-F1 on the BAH public evaluation split, outperforming both global visual-face token fusion and synchronized evidence baselines.
AI.conclusion: Synchronized visual-facial cross-refinement with pairwise multimodal evidence fusion effectively improves ambivalence and hesitancy recognition over baseline fusion strategies.

title: All you need is SAMPAT
summary: The current state of the art in AI/ML rests on deep neural architectures, which, in general, suffer from a lack of interpretability. Interpretability is crucial to gleaning insights while analyzing experimental data, where quantitative predictions may not be adequate for a scientist. We present a three layer neural architecture, SAMPAT (Smooth Approximation via Multivariate Polynomials and Analytic Transformations), that can provably learn a continuous, everywhere differentiable function, that can approximate any smooth function arbitrarily closely. SAMPAT's approximant can be expressed as a closed and compact algebraic, analytic expression, providing complete interpretability. Experiments on synthetic and benchmark datasets indicate that SAMPAT yields competitive performance with simpler representations. For many tasks, a two layer SAMPAT suffices. By imposing restrictions on the connectivity between neurons, SAMPAT may be used to provide a range of approximants, including regular and trigonometric polynomials, rational expressions, Gaussians, mixtures of Gaussians, as well as arbitrary combinations of the same; without restrictions, it learns a suitable structure. SAMPAT may be used to factorize polynomials and model nonlinear systems. With the addition of skip connections, a 4 to 6 layer SAMPAT is adequate to represent a substantive range of methods widely used in AI/ML, allowing the choice of a model's family, not just its parameters, to also be optimized as part of the learning process.

AI.tldr: SAMPAT is a three-layer neural architecture that learns smooth, interpretable functions via closed-form algebraic/analytic expressions, achieving competitive performance while enabling model family selection as part of optimization.
AI.motivation: Deep neural networks lack interpretability, which is crucial for scientific data analysis where quantitative predictions alone are insufficient for gaining insights.
AI.method: A three-layer neural architecture (SAMPAT) based on smooth approximation via multivariate polynomials and analytic transformations, with optional connectivity restrictions and skip connections.
AI.result: SAMPAT achieves competitive performance on synthetic and benchmark datasets; two layers suffice for many tasks; with skip connections, 4-6 layers can represent a wide range of AI/ML methods.
AI.conclusion: SAMPAT provides complete interpretability through closed-form expressions while allowing optimization over model family, not just parameters, and can represent diverse approximants including polynomials, rational functions, and Gaussians.

title: Multimodal Scenario Similarity Search for Autonomous Driving
